newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN approves new rights investigator for Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: UN approves new rights investigator for Nigeria.

text.p: The U.N. Human Rights Commission agreed on Tuesday to appoint a special investigator into allegations of major abuses in Nigeria, including arbitrary detentions and summary executions.

In the resolution adopted by the 53-member forum, it also called on the Lagos government to guarantee fundamental freedoms and release "all prisoners, trade union leaders, human rights advocates and journalists currently detained".
The text urges Nigeria to ensure that all trials are held fairly and promptly in conformity with international standards.

The main U.N. human rights forum was widely expected to censure Nigeria at this year's session by naming a specific "country rapporteur" or investigator for Africa's most populous nation and an OPEC member.

Two "thematic" special U.N. rapporteurs (investigators), those looking into independence of judges and lawyers, and extrajudical or arbitrary executions, called for naming an investigator for Nigeria in their latest report this month.

They called off a mission to Nigeria in Feburary due to a last-minute row with the government over access to detainees, according to the latest report by the rapporteurs, Malaysian lawyer Param Cumaraswamy and Senegal's Bacre Waly Ndiaye.
The vote was 28 states in favour of the resolution, six states against with 19 abstentions. Nigeria is not a member at this year's Commission, which has a rotating membership.
